name: WIRED
look: Paper-white broadsheet density, three-face serif and sans system, square buttons, ink-blue links.

hero.title: The engineers who quietly rebuilt the grid
hero.sub: For six years a team of forty worked on a problem nobody wanted to fund. Then the lights stayed on, and everybody wanted to know how.

features.title: Six stories from the March edition
features.sub: Reported over four continents across the last eleven weeks.

items.title: The grid rebuilders
items.body: Forty engineers, six years, and the unglamorous work of keeping the lights on in a warming world.

items.title: The breach nobody reported
items.body: A three-year intrusion at a supplier nobody had heard of, and the disclosure rules that let it stay quiet.

items.title: Editing the wheat
items.body: A gene-edited grain is about to reach European fields. The science is settled; the politics are not.

items.title: The cable wars
items.body: Ninety-eight percent of intercontinental traffic runs through cables owned by fewer companies each year.

items.title: What the models forgot
items.body: A generation of climate models agreed on the average and missed the tails. The tails arrived first.

items.title: The last darkroom
items.body: In a basement in Lisbon, four printers keep a craft alive that the industry declared finished in 2009.

showcases.title: The breach nobody reported
showcases.body: For three years an intruder sat inside a components supplier serving eleven national utilities. Disclosure rules did not require anyone to say so, and nobody did. Our reporters reconstructed the intrusion from court filings and four sources inside the company.
points: Four sources, three on the record
Timeline verified against three incident reports

showcases.title: Editing the wheat
showcases.body: A gene-edited grain resistant to a fungus that costs European farmers a billion euros a year is weeks from approval. The science has been settled since 2021. The argument has not.

notes: A strict black-and-white duet. The only chromatic element in the whole system is the inline link blue.
Three faces do three jobs: a display serif for headlines, a text serif for body, and a sans reserved for metadata, bylines and buttons.
Buttons are square. The brand never softens a corner on an interactive element.
The story grid is the layout: a large feature at the top, a two-up below it, then bylined rows separated by 1px hairlines.
The masthead band — a thin black strip with the wordmark centred — is the only decorative move in the system.
